create.name: Plum Village App
create.bio:
The Plum Village App brings the practice of the Plum Village tradition, the Zen community founded by Thich Nhat Hanh, to phones and computers at no cost. Thay, as his students call him, had imagined an online monastery where people could feel what it is like to practise in one of his centres from wherever they are, and the app is offered as a step towards that idea. It is produced by a small team working closely with the monastic community in France and published by the Centre for Applied Ethics.

Inside are hundreds of recordings: guided sitting meditations, total relaxations, chanting by monks and nuns, the cheerful practice songs familiar to anyone who has been on a Plum Village retreat, and a large archive of Thich Nhat Hanh answering questions put to him by students. Teachings cover everyday mindfulness, eating and walking meditation, and caring for strong emotions. There is a web version, and browser extensions show one of Thay's calligraphies in each new tab. Everything is free, with no paid tier; the work is funded by donors, including a monthly giving circle called the Oak Forest Family. The team also publishes regular news of new content and app releases on its blog.

courses.title: The Oak Forest Family
courses.description: A monthly giving circle that keeps the app and its content free for everyone. Supporters choose a level that covers running costs or helps fund new recordings and features; one-off gifts are also possible.
